note: Views Block Area adds two Views handlers via hook_views_data(): an area handler 'views_block_area' (Global: Block area, usable in header/footer/no-results) and a field handler 'views_block_field' (Content block: Block Field). Both render an arbitrary non-context-aware block plugin, with options block_id, block_title, hide_label, empty. There is no settings form or configure route; configuration lives inside each view's display config. Medium/hard cases build/read namespaced vba_* views whose displays carry these handlers, verified by loading the View config entity via drush. Context-aware blocks are excluded from the selectable list.

evals.prompt: What does the views_block_area module add to Views, and which two handler ids does it provide?
evals.expected_output: It exposes any block plugin inside a view. It provides an area handler 'views_block_area' (Global: Block area, for header/footer/no-results) and a field handler 'views_block_field' (Content block: Block Field).

evals.prompt: Using views_block_area, how do I put a block into a view's header or footer, and what options can I set on it?
evals.expected_output: Edit the view, click Add next to Header (or Footer / No results behavior), choose 'Global: Block area', and pick the block. Options: block_id (which block), block_title (title override), hide_label, and empty (render even with no results).

evals.prompt: Which kind of blocks does views_block_area NOT let you select, and why?
evals.expected_output: Context-aware blocks (block definitions with a 'context' key) are excluded from the selectable list because a view cannot supply the runtime context they require. Broken blocks and block_content derivatives whose content entity is gone also render as nothing.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a view (machine name vba_known) that uses views_block_area to place a block in its header. Inspect the view's configuration and state the block plugin id (block_id) it renders in the header.
evals.expected_output: The vba_known view's default display header has a views_block_area handler with block_id: system_powered_by_block. Read it with `drush cget views.view.vba_known` or by loading the View entity.

evals.prompt: This site has a view (machine name vba_fld) that uses the views_block_area 'Block field' handler to render a block as a field. Inspect the view configuration and report which block plugin id it shows.
evals.expected_output: The vba_fld view has a views_block_field field handler with block_id: system_branding_block. Discoverable via `drush cget views.view.vba_fld`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a view with machine name vba_task. Using the views_block_area module, add a Block area to this view (e.g. in its footer) that renders the core 'Powered by Drupal' block (block plugin id system_powered_by_block). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The vba_task view has a views_block_area handler (header/footer/empty) with block_id: system_powered_by_block.

evals.prompt: The view vba_field_task on this site needs the site's branding block shown as a field in its results. Using the views_block_area 'Block field' handler, add the core Site branding block (block plugin id system_branding_block) as a field on the vba_field_task view, and apply it live.
evals.expected_output: The vba_field_task view has a views_block_field field handler with block_id: system_branding_block.
